transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I… I came in because I just can’t shake this heavy feeling. Like this hopeless weight, you know? Ever since the divorce I kept trying to rebuild things—work, the apartment, routines, all of it—and now it feels like everything I built has just collapsed, and I’m sitting underneath it.

Sorry, that sounds dramatic. I’m an engineer, so I keep thinking of it like a structure failing, which is probably not helpful, but… that’s how it feels. Like I’m trapped under the debris and I don’t know how to get out.
Did this heavy, hopeless feeling start after the divorce?

Sort of… not right after the divorce itself, exactly. It’s been more like the past month that it’s really been hanging over me.

The divorce set things off, I guess, but the financial mess afterward—sorting accounts, bills, realizing what I could and couldn’t afford—that’s when it really sank in. I remember looking at this spreadsheet I made, color-coded and everything, like somehow formatting it nicely would make it less awful, and it just… didn’t. Since around then, it’s been there almost every day.
Do these feelings seem mainly connected to the financial fallout from the divorce?

I mean… the money part is definitely wrapped up in it, but it’s bigger than just finances. It’s like after the divorce I kept trying to rebuild everything piece by piece, like if I just made a plan and followed it, I’d be okay. And now it feels like all of that collapsed anyway.

Sorry, I keep going back to construction metaphors—it’s just how my brain works. But the feeling is this heavy, hopeless thing, like I’m stuck under everything that fell apart and I can’t really get out from under it.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t know… I mean, I guess I haven’t really thought about it that way. I’ve still been doing some things, but it’s hard to tell if I’m enjoying them or just… going through the motions.

Like, I used to spend ages messing with little design projects at home—totally unnecessary stuff, like reorganizing a shelf so it “distributes load better,” which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud. And lately I’ll start something and then get distracted by, I don’t know, a bill sitting on the counter or an email I forgot to answer, and then suddenly I’m cleaning a drawer I didn’t need to clean.

So… I’m not sure. Maybe? I just don’t feel very connected to much right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… most days, I think so. It’s this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t seem to shake.

I came in because it feels like everything I tried to build back up after the divorce just collapsed, and I’m kind of… sitting underneath it. Like when a structure fails and you can see afterward there were too many loads on it, too many weak points, but knowing that doesn’t actually get you out from under the rubble. So yes, I guess—down, depressed, whatever word fits—it’s there a lot of the day.
Has this been making it hard for you to function at work?

Yeah… it has. More than I wanted to admit at first.

Work used to be the place where I could sort of hold myself together because there were drawings and numbers and decisions that had a process, you know? But lately I’ve been making calls I probably shouldn’t have been making—questionable ones—and then I’d realize afterward I wasn’t thinking clearly. And meetings… I’ve just kind of fallen apart in them. Not in some dramatic movie way, just losing the thread, getting overwhelmed, not being able to answer things I should know.

My supervisor actually took me off active project decisions, which was humiliating. I mean, I get why. You can’t have someone unstable making calls about loads and safety and budgets and all that. Sorry, that’s probably too much detail.

And at home it’s not better. I stopped keeping up with basic routines, like the normal maintenance stuff of being a person. It got bad enough that I ended up being sent to the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like after the divorce especially, but I don’t know if it was “depressed like this” or if it lasted exactly two weeks. I’m bad with timelines unless I can anchor them to a project deadline or something concrete.

There were times I wasn’t doing great, definitely, but this feels… heavier? Or maybe I’m just remembering it that way because I’m in it now. Sorry, I’m kind of circling the question. I don’t really know how to answer that clearly.
Before this past month, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed like this nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I honestly don’t know. I can remember being really low at different points, but whether it was nearly every day for two full weeks before this past month… I can’t say clearly.

It’s weird, because I can remember details like which bridge inspection report was late or what color folder I used for a permit set, but my own mood timeline is just blurry. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m just filling in gaps. I’m not sure.
If the divorce and financial fallout were suddenly resolved, do you think this depressed feeling would still be there?

I think… yes. I mean, if the money stuff and the divorce mess magically disappeared, I’d obviously be relieved, but I don’t think this feeling would just lift.

That’s kind of why I came in. I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like everything I tried to build back up after the divorce has collapsed anyway, and I’m just sitting underneath it. And it’s hard to explain because part of me wants to say, “Well, of course I’m upset, look at the circumstances,” but it feels bigger than that. Like it would still be there even if someone fixed the practical pieces.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?

Yeah… I mean, not like I have some neat answer to that. I’ve been having these thoughts that it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Like if I could just not have to keep doing all of this.

And it scared me, honestly. It got intense enough that I called the employee assistance program through work, which was embarrassing because I kept thinking about how I’ve used EAP for workplace trainings before, like those little posters in the break room that everyone ignores… but then I was the person calling. So… yes, I guess the answer is yes.
Do you feel more hopeless than you would expect someone to feel just because of the divorce and financial problems?

Yes. I think it’s more than what I’d expect from just the divorce and money stuff.

I mean, those things are terrible, obviously, and I could make a whole spreadsheet of the practical reasons I’m stressed — I’ve always done that, lists and budgets and little color-coded tabs, which probably sounds ridiculous — but this feels different. Heavier.

That’s why I came in. I can’t shake this hopeless feeling, like everything I tried to build after the divorce just collapsed, and I’m sitting under it. Even if the external stuff explains part of it, it doesn’t feel like the whole explanation.
Before this past month, have you ever had a time in your life when you felt depressed like this almost every day for at least two weeks?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve ever sat down and counted it out as “two weeks” before, you know?

There have been bad stretches, definitely. Like after big life stuff, or when work got really overwhelming — civil projects can drag on forever and everyone acts like concrete cures faster if they send more emails — but whether it was this kind of depressed almost every day for two full weeks… I don’t know. I’d have to think about it more. This past month feels different enough that it’s hard for me to compare.
At any time before this past month, did you ever have a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

I still don’t really know. I’m trying to think back and it’s like… my memory turns into this messy filing cabinet, you know? I can remember being sad or overwhelmed before, but whether it was nearly every day for two weeks, exactly… I can’t say for sure.

I keep thinking of certain work periods, or after things changed in my personal life, but then I start second-guessing myself because some days I functioned fine, or at least looked like I did. So… I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I’m honestly not sure.
Before this past month, do you remember any time in your life when you were depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m sorry, I know I’m probably not answering this cleanly. I don’t remember a clear time before now where I can confidently say, yes, that was nearly every day for at least two weeks.

I can remember periods where I was low or just… dragging through things, especially when life got complicated, but then I start thinking about work deadlines or random days where I was distracted enough to seem fine. Like I’d be on-site arguing about drainage calculations and everyone would think I was functioning, so does that count as not depressed that day? I don’t know.

So I guess the honest answer is: I’m not sure. I don’t have a specific two-week stretch before this past month that I can point to.
Before this past month, do you remember ever having another episode of depression that was clearly separate from this one?

I don’t think I can say that clearly. Like, “separate episode” sounds very organized, and my life has not felt organized like that.

There were times I was down before, sure, but I can’t point to one and say, okay, that was a separate depression episode and then it ended and now this is a new one. It’s more like… patches of bad weather, I guess, and sometimes I was still going to work and answering emails and dealing with contractors, so it all blurs together.

So no clear separate episode comes to mind. I’m not saying it definitely never happened, I just don’t remember one clearly.
